nieves_body_tuning.name: Body Fitting
nieves_body_tuning.system.description:
She adjusts her own body as calmly as anyone else's: the layers under the skin thicken, and a blow sinks into the meat without reaching the bone.

Effect: +2 DR to herself for 6 rounds.

In the scene: explains why she doesn't go down from the first blow. Cast before combat, if Nieves had time to hear footsteps.

nieves_grafting.name: Graft
nieves_grafting.system.description:
Someone else's trait, grafted on the fly: the Matriarch's skin coarsens and sprouts horny growths right in the middle of the fight.

Effect: the Thick Skin adaptation: DR 1 against slashing and piercing, for Doctrine Rank rounds (3). A willing target makes no saving throw; an unwilling one rolls Willpower against DC 12.

In the scene: a test of the Adaptation Modifier on the GM's side. Applied with a button on the card.

nieves_stitching.name: Stitch-Up
nieves_stitching.system.description:
Nieves doesn't heal, she mends. Torn flesh closes with a stitch no one put in, and the seam lies exactly where she looks.

In the scene: her whole turn. While she is alive and can see the Matriarch, the boss fight doesn't end: that is the answer to the question “why should the party go after the witch behind bars.”

shadow_dead_tongue.name: Dead Tongue
shadow_dead_tongue.system.description:
Long cast. Doctrine Rank 1. Time: 1 hour. Component: a corpse no more than [Doctrine Rank] days old.

Out of combat only. Costs no AP. One long cast between Long Rests. Requires a magical focus.

The shadowmancer pries open the dead person's mouth, cuts their own palm, and lays it on the corpse's tongue. The corpse speaks in the mage's voice, moving someone else's jaw.

  • The corpse answers [Doctrine Rank] questions.
  • It knows only what it knew in life and saw with its own eyes. Of what happened after its death it knows nothing.
  • It doesn't guess or interpret: it answers literally.
  • Personality remains: a liar lies, a stubborn one keeps silent, a fool gets confused.

The dead answer once and for all. This corpse won't speak a second time, not for this mage or any other. The body is a consumable.

The cost. For a day, the mage tastes whatever the corpse ate on the last day of its life. Until a Long Rest: −2 to Persuasion and Performance.

shadow_false_life.name: False Life
shadow_false_life.system.description:
Long cast. Doctrine Rank 2. Time: 1 hour. Component: a fresh corpse no more than a day old.

Out of combat only. Costs no AP. One long cast between Long Rests. Requires a magical focus.

The mage strips the flesh from a dead body and drives it into the target. The corpse is used up entirely; only skin and bones remain. The wounds close over in gray, someone else's; the seams don't match in color.

  • The target gains temporary HP equal to 25% of their maximum HP. They last until a Long Rest.
  • Dead flesh doesn't heal. While False Life is in effect, the target cannot regain HP by any means: not by Biomancy, potions, a Healing check, or rest.
  • To end it early, cut open the seams: Interact with a Healing check. The temporary HP are lost entirely.

The cost. The target looks like a walking corpse: ashen skin, the smell of decay.

Apply the False Life condition to the target; the healing ban isn't automated and is enforced by the GM.

shadow_severed_shade.name: Severed Shade
shadow_severed_shade.system.description:
Long cast. Doctrine Rank 2. Time: 1 hour. Component: a corpse or a place where someone died.

Out of combat only. Costs no AP. One long cast between Long Rests. Requires a magical focus.

The mage traces the outline of the body on the ground with a knife and cuts the shadow from the spot like a hide. It is voiceless and will-less, and recognizable: it is the shadow of a specific dead person, with their silhouette, hunch, and limp.

It lasts [Doctrine Rank] × 10 minutes or until dawn, whichever comes first.

The mode is chosen at casting, one per cast:

  • Scouting. The mage sees and hears through what the shadow sees. It goes up to [Doctrine Rank] × 20 meters and passes anywhere a person could, but doesn't open doors or touch objects. While the mage looks through its eyes, they are blind and deaf to their own body and lie where they lay down.
  • Apparition. The shadow rises before a chosen target. Willpower saving throw, DC 8 + 2 × Doctrine Rank. Failure: Fear; at Doctrine Rank 4 and higher, Terror.
  • Distraction. The shadow makes noise and flickers off to the side. Everything that could notice it looks that way for [Doctrine Rank] rounds: the group gets +[Doctrine Rank] to one Stealth check or slips past a post without a roll; the GM decides.

The cost. The shadow obeys imprecisely. Once per cast the GM may let it do something its own way: something the dead person did in life. And it is recognizable: if someone who knew the deceased sees the shadow, there will be consequences.
